original_question: Let U^*_X(k) be the moduli space of semistable vector bundles on X of rank k and degree k(g-1), let Θ_k = { F in U^*_X(k) | h^0(X, F) ≠ 0 }, and let M = O(Θ_k). For the tensor-product map τ_{k,r}: SU_X(r) × U^*_X(k) → U^*_X(kr), the pullback of the canonical theta divisor defines a linear map ϑ_{k,r}: H^0(SU_X(r), L^k) → H^0(U^*_X(k), M^r)^*. Is ϑ_{k,r} always an isomorphism, equivalently, is |L^k| spanned by the divisors Θ_F = { E in SU_X(r) | h^0(X, E ⊗ F) ≠ 0 } as F ranges over U^*_X(k)?
target_in_paper: Section 8, Question 6 (Beauville’s strange duality conjecture), together with its explicit geometric reformulation Question 6′.
correct_elements: Your draft is very close to the paper’s actual target. It correctly identifies the moduli space U_X^*(k), the canonical theta divisor Θ_k, the line bundle M = O(Θ_k), the tensor-product morphism τ_{k,r}, the induced strange-duality map ϑ_{k,r}, and the paper’s equivalent geometric reformulation in terms of spanning |L^k| by the divisors Θ_F. It is also correctly scoped to the fixed-degree case treated in Beauville’s Section 8, rather than the broader arbitrary-degree extension only mentioned in passing.
missing_details: The paper works with X a compact Riemann surface, and Beauville states that he implicitly assumes genus g ≥ 2 throughout.
The quantifiers on r and k should be explicit: the conjecture is for all positive integers r and k.
SU_X(r) should be defined explicitly as the moduli space of semistable rank-r vector bundles on X with trivial determinant.
The line bundle L on SU_X(r) should be defined: for any A in J^{g-1}(X), Θ_A = {E in SU_X(r) | h^0(X, E ⊗ A) ≥ 1}, and L = O(Θ_A), independent of the choice of A.
The paper’s strange-duality map has the direction ϑ_{k,r}: H^0(U_X^*(k), M^r)^* → H^0(SU_X(r), L^k), not the reverse direction written in the draft.
Beauville emphasizes that ϑ_{k,r} is only well-defined up to a scalar, because it comes from the divisor of a section cutting out τ_{k,r}^*Θ_{kr}.

The equivalence with the spanning statement is not formal from the definition alone; it uses Beauville’s argument that the two vector spaces have the same dimension, obtained in Section 8(b) via the Verlinde formula.

If one wants the question to be fully stand-alone, one should state that U_X^*(k) is the moduli space of semistable vector bundles of rank k and degree k(g−1), carrying the canonical theta divisor Θ_k = {F | h^0(X, F) ≠ 0}.
refined_question: Let X be a compact Riemann surface of genus g ≥ 2, and let r, k ≥ 1. Let SU_X(r) denote the moduli space of semistable rank-r vector bundles on X with trivial determinant, and let L = O(Θ_A) be its determinant line bundle, where for any A ∈ J^{g−1}(X) one sets Θ_A = {E ∈ SU_X(r) | h^0(X, E ⊗ A) ≥ 1}. Let U_X^*(k) be the moduli space of semistable vector bundles on X of rank k and degree k(g−1), with canonical theta divisor Θ_k = {F ∈ U_X^*(k) | h^0(X, F) ≠ 0} and M = O(Θ_k). For the tensor-product morphism τ_{k,r}: SU_X(r) × U_X^*(k) → U_X^*(kr), (E, F) ↦ E ⊗ F, the divisor τ_{k,r}^*Θ_{kr} defines, up to scalar, a linear map ϑ_{k,r}: H^0(U_X^*(k), M^r)^* → H^0(SU_X(r), L^k). Is ϑ_{k,r} an isomorphism for every X, r, and k?
equivalent_formulation: Equivalently: is the linear system |L^k| on SU_X(r) spanned by the divisors Θ_F = {E ∈ SU_X(r) | h^0(X, E ⊗ F) ≠ 0} as F ranges over U_X^*(k)?
justification: The draft is targeting Beauville’s Section 8 exactly: his official formulation is Question 6, 'Conjecture: The map ϑ_{k,r} is an isomorphism' (Section 8, p. 29). Beauville then immediately gives the equivalent geometric reformulation as Question 6′, namely that |L^k| is spanned by the divisors Θ_F (Section 8, p. 29). To make the question fully stand-alone and faithful to the paper, one must restore the ambient setup from earlier sections: X is a compact Riemann surface with the standing implicit assumption g ≥ 2 (Section 1, p. 19), SU_X(r) is the moduli space of semistable rank-r bundles with trivial determinant, and L is the determinant bundle defined from the divisors Θ_A (Section 2, pp. 19–20). The draft’s main mathematical mismatch is the direction of ϑ_{k,r}: in the paper it is H^0(U_X^*(k), M^r)^* → H^0(SU_X(r), L^k), not the reverse. Also, Beauville specifies that the map is only defined up to scalar, and the equivalence with the spanning formulation uses his equal-dimension argument in Section 8(b), which invokes the Verlinde formula from Theorem 5 (Section 5, p. 23; Section 8, p. 29).
